coverageNote: Enumerated from disk: 7 units (the domain directory itself + 6 sub-domain directories, each containing an *-index.md), 38 .md files. Matches the expected 7 units / 38 files exactly; no orphan files outside a unit directory. Every file was read in full through the 3a (implementer simulation) -> 3b (rubric scoring) -> 3c (devil's advocate) cycle. Cross-checks were run against meta/constraints.md (jurisdiction/compliance ratifications D-72 and the US-first revision) because two units cite it normatively; that file is outside this domain and was read only as a referenced constraint, not audited. A programmatic relative-link check found 3 dead cross-domain directory references (01.01.01:181 -> ../../18-show-production/, 01.06.01:191 -> ../../08-real-time-jamming/, 01.06.01:195 -> ../../20-fanbase-community/); these are reference hygiene, not ambiguity that changes what gets built, and are recorded here rather than as findings. Devil's-advocate pass dropped 4 candidate findings that did not survive: (a) 01.01-cx CX-02 co-owner-alias staleness, because 01.01.02:135 explicitly records both sub-questions as dissolved; (b) 01.02-cx CX-03 stale divergent-terminal-state marker, because 01.02.02 D-17/DT-15 resolves it and names the CX file; (c) 01.05.03 D-05 'credits never transfer with a party' vs 01.01.02 D-03's ownership-period model, because the ownership-period model delivers exactly D-05's stated intent; (d) 01.03.03 D-07's decision text omitting the `permanent` qualifier, because the rule table, D-09 and every cross-reference in the tree state it unambiguously.

dimensionApplicability.note: Dimensions 1 (Problem Clarity), 2 (Persona Specificity) and 6 (Competitive Positioning) are N/A across every unit in this domain: problem-statement.md, personas.md and competitive-landscape.md own them, and every Role Matrix in this tree carries the explicit rule 'NEVER redefine a persona here - reference only'. Dimension 4 (Constraint Explicitness) is applicable only where the unit sets constraint values of its own (the domain root via 01.07/01.08 jurisdiction compliance; 01.02 via 01.02.01 D-14's regime-profile parameterisation; 01.05 via 01.05.01/01.05.02's numeric abuse and challenge defaults) and N/A elsewhere, where the axes are owned by meta/constraints.md and referenced. Dimensions 3, 5, 7 and 8 are applicable in every unit.

findings.failureScenario: Implementer A builds the Record layer and the EPK from 01.06.01/01.06.03 and renders each credit as "Drums on 'Song' — attested by Sam Reeves". Implementer B builds them from 01.06.02 D-02 and renders "Drums on 'Song' — confirmed by 3 people who were there". These are different products on the platform's most-visited surface. The 01.06.03 case is the worst instance: D-03 requires the EPK to work for "a recipient with no account, on a phone" and D-06 makes the per-recipient link "a tracking wrapper over public content, not an access gate", so building it per 01.06.03 step 5 publishes the full attester graph to any forwarded stranger — precisely the outcome 01.06.02 D-02 says "hands a scraper the moat" and "turns a private act into a public endorsement". 01.06.01 D-18 is worse still: it makes the attester's name part of the reel caption, which 01.06.01 DT-08 separately identifies as the caption that "identifies the infringing use, the work, and the rightsholder to serve". No file carries a marker, a deferral or a superseding note; 01.06.02 (updated 2026-07-23) simply post-dates 01.06.01 and 01.06.03 (2026-07-16 and 2026-07-17) and the reconciliation was never propagated.

findings.forcedInvention: What a provisional owner may do when adding a member to a band party — whether member-adding is barred outright, whether added members are exempted from the ratified peer seed, or whether the seed applies and the stated prohibition is simply violated. No text in the tree decides it.
findings.claim: 01.05.02's provisional-control powers table permits adding members without signing authority and, in the adjacent cell, forbids adding a member with one. For a band party those two cells are jointly unsatisfiable, because 01.03.03 D-07's ratified peer seed grants `sign` automatically to every confirmed permanent member.
findings.evidence: 01.05.02-claim-initiation-proof-methods.md:80 — the powers table row, both cells: "| Add members/mandates **without** signing authority | Grant a **signing mandate** or add a member with one (01.03) — a laundering route |". 01.05.02-claim-initiation-proof-methods.md:231 — D-08: "**Provisional control may do anything the platform can undo, and nothing it cannot** | DT-07. Closes the gap left open at sub-domain CX-02 note 3. A derivation rule, not a list". — CONTRADICTED BY — 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:40 — the ratified default rule table: "| **Peer seed** (D-07) | Every **`confirmed`** membership edge whose current capacity period is `permanent` carries the **full seven-activity set**"; 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:47 — "**Confirmation is the moment authority arrives.** ... acceptance now *is* a grant of authority"; 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:25 — the seven activities: "a closed set of **seven**: book / sign / spend / list / release / settle / administer (D-01, ratified at DQ-02.3)".
findings.failureScenario: A provisional owner of a band party (granted on Tier B proof from a single attester — 01.05.02 D-07) invites a confederate as a permanent member. The confederate confirms. Under 01.03.03 D-07 the confirmation seeds them with all seven activities including `sign` and `administer`, so the provisional owner has done exactly what 01.05.02's own table calls "a laundering route", using only the permission the same table grants. The confederate can then sign and administer before the 01.05.03 reversibility window closes, and 01.05.03 D-03's reversibility — the sole reason 01.05.02 D-02 can offer weak-but-fast proof at all — no longer bounds the blast radius. An implementer must invent one of three unstated rules to proceed: bar provisional owners from adding members entirely (breaking nothing stated but contradicting the 'may' cell), exempt provisional-added members from the peer seed (inventing a second seeding model), or add members only at `touring`/`staff` capacity (an inference no text makes — 01.03.03 D-09 keys the seed to capacity but nothing connects that to provisional control). Nothing in 01.05.02's Open Questions, 01.05.03's, or 01.03.03's covers this: 01.05.02 was last updated 2026-07-16, before the DQ-02.4 seed ratification, and was never revisited.

findings.forcedInvention: How the USD 1,000 per-act value ceiling applies to an act that carries no monetary value — whether unvalued acts are treated as zero-value (always permitted), as unbounded (always escalated), or are exempt from the ceiling entirely. Four of the seven seeded verbs routinely have no monetary value, and the ceiling is their only stated bound.
findings.claim: The ratified band default bounds all seven seeded activities by a per-act figure denominated in money, but `administer`, `list`, `release` and non-monetary `book` acts have no monetary value, and no text defines how the bound resolves for them. The tree then states the unbounded reading as fact in three places without ever deriving it.
findings.evidence: 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:41 — the ceiling rule: "| **Value ceiling** (D-08) | Seeded authority is capped at **USD 1,000 per act**, configurable per band. Acts above the ceiling escalate to the owning-mandate holder, who is uncapped | Band orgs |". 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:48 — stated with no ceiling qualification at all: "**The seed includes `administer`.** Any confirmed permanent member can therefore alter another member's mandate, invite, and remove." 01.03-membership-representation-mandate-cx.md:35 — CX-01 note 3, also unqualified: "**Widened by 01.03.03 D-07**: in a band, `administer` is seeded on every confirmed permanent edge, so the recursion is peer-to-peer rather than creator-down — any permanent member may alter any other's mandate." 01.03.02-representation-roster-relationships.md:46 — the opposite framing, ceiling applied to a non-monetary act: "for a band, *any* `confirmed` `permanent` member can accept, because `sign` and `administer` are seeded — subject to the USD 1,000 per-act ceiling, above which it escalates to the uncapped owning-mandate holder". 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:64 — the escalation edge case presumes every act has a comparable value: "| Action exceeds the mandate's value ceiling | Blocked at the call site (cross-cut) and **escalated** ... every seeded mandate carries the USD 1,000 ceiling, so there is always a threshold to exceed |".
findings.failureScenario: A four-piece band runs on the default. The drummer opens the people surface and removes the guitarist from the band. Implementer A, reading 01.03.03 line 48 and 01.03-cx line 35 literally, permits it: removal has no monetary value, the ceiling cannot be exceeded, so any permanent member may remove any other. Implementer B, reading 01.03.02 line 46's framing that even accepting representation is 'subject to the USD 1,000 per-act ceiling', treats an unvalued act as unbounded and escalates it to the uncapped owning-mandate holder — so only the band's creator can remove anyone. The same divergence decides whether any permanent member can unilaterally appoint the band's manager for two years worldwide (01.03.02 Happy Path), publish a release (`release`), or add a `shop` type and thereby incur statutory trader duties (01.02.03 / 01.08). These are the highest-stakes acts in the domain, and 01.03.03's own Edge Cases (line 69) concede there is "no pre-act gate below the ceiling" while never saying what 'below the ceiling' means for an act with no price. No tracked question covers it: Q-03 asks whether the flat ceiling should become the band's own agreed threshold (still monetary), and Q-04 asks what a representation edge's ceiling is when unset (a different dimension, explicitly scoped to representation edges).

A second implementer, following D-04 first, builds only single-owner alias contexts and no shared-alias presence indicator at all. The divergence is not merely dead code — 01.01.03:34's phrase 'subject to 01.01.02 Q-01' instructs the implementer to treat the alias ownership model as undecided, which is the one thing the domain has decided three times over (01.01.02 D-04, sub-domain index Q-02, domain index Q-08). Both files carry the same Last-updated date of 2026-07-23, so this is not simple staleness; the ratification was propagated into 01.01.02 and never into 01.01.03.

Under the ratified band seed the two readings differ by the entire band.

findings.failureScenario: A four-piece band on the default wants to self-release. Implementer A maps 'owner/admin' onto the `administer` activity, so any confirmed permanent member may add the `label` type — and equally may add `shop`, which 01.02.03's own Edge Cases (line 50) and 01.02.02's Cross-Cut Notes state re-triggers 01.08's trader assessment and its statutory publication duty. Implementer B maps 'owner/admin' onto the uncapped owning mandate, so only the band's creator may do it — which reintroduces exactly the creator-privilege asymmetry 01.03.03 DT-03 refused to invent and 01.02.02 D-07 was amended to remove. 01.02.03 DT-04's stated rationale ('Otherwise a session player linked to a studio could unilaterally make it a shop') is satisfied by both readings for a studio, where nothing is seeded, and by neither cleanly for a band, where everyone is a peer. The unit's own Q-04-adjacent question (01.02.01 Q-04) narrows a different problem — whether an explicit grant can be scoped per type — and does not name this gate.

findings.failureScenario: An implementer building the v1 US listing flow must decide whether the trader/private classification gate exists at launch. Reading 01.08 D-04 alone they build a blocking pre-publish declaration flow rendering 'this seller is a private individual; consumer protections do not apply' — copy whose premise (a withdrawal right the buyer is losing) constraints.md says does not exist federally in the US. Reading the domain's own ratified pattern — an unauthored profile resolves statutory fields to explicit `unknown` (01.07 D-06, 01.02.01 D-14) — they resolve the classification to `undetermined` at launch and ship no gate, which under 01.08 D-04's fail-closed rule would mean nobody can list anything. The file's Q-02 asks only whether the classification *varies* by jurisdiction and is deferred to /create-prd-security; it does not ask which profile is authored at launch, and it does not mark D-04's gate as contingent on the answer. This is a stale constraint premise rather than a missing decision: the reconciliation was performed for 01.07 and 01.02.01 and never propagated here.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether a membership edge whose current capacity period carries both `permanent` and a non-seeded capacity is seeded or not. 01.03.01's own worked example creates exactly that state; 01.03.03's seed rule is written as though a period carries one capacity.
findings.claim: 01.03.01 models a member holding two capacities in one period ('permanent + staff'), while 01.03.03's ratified seed keys on 'whose current capacity period is `permanent`' in the singular and gives `staff` zero authority. Nothing states how a compound capacity resolves.
findings.evidence: 01.03.01-membership-records-lifecycle.md:63 — Happy Path step 9: "Two years on, the drummer's role changes: they take over front-of-house on the band's own shows. Their capacity period `permanent (2026–2028)` closes and **`permanent + staff (2028–)`** opens. Tenure is unbroken; the capacity history is a list." — against — 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:40 — "| **Peer seed** (D-07) | Every **`confirmed`** membership edge **whose current capacity period is `permanent`** carries the **full seven-activity set** |"; 01.03.03-mandate-scope-delegated-authority.md:42 — D-09: "| **Capacity keying** (D-09) | The seed attaches to `permanent` only. `touring`, `staff` and `honorary` carry **presence with zero authority** until something is granted explicitly |"; 01.03.01-membership-records-lifecycle.md:81 — stated at edge level rather than period level: "`touring`, `staff` and `honorary` **edges** are **outside the peer seed** — they carry presence with zero authority and therefore no acting context for the band until the band grants something explicitly".
findings.failureScenario: The drummer in 01.03.01's own Happy Path takes on front-of-house and their capacity period becomes 'permanent + staff'. Implementer A reads 01.03.03's rule as satisfied by any `permanent` component and keeps the full seven-activity seed. Implementer B reads 01.03.01:81's edge-level phrasing — an edge carrying `staff` is 'outside the peer seed' — and revokes the seed, so a founding member silently loses all band authority and their acting context (01.01.03 line 42) disappears the moment they agree to run sound. The second outcome is a silent loss of authority, which 01.03-cx CX-01 note 4 classifies as a security-grade event requiring notification, and it happens with nobody having made any decision. The Behavior table's phrasing (01.03.01:34, 'permanent / touring / staff / honorary, each with its own date range') supports the compound reading; 01.03.03's rule is written for the singular. Neither 01.03.01 Q-02 (which explicitly narrows to a representation choice with 'no behavioral difference') nor 01.03.03's questions cover it.

findings.evidence: 01.03.01-membership-records-lifecycle.md:162 — D-03, the enum with its explicit closure history: "| D-03 | Capacity is on the edge (**permanent / touring / staff / honorary**), not on the person | `session` **removed** from the enum per D-05 — a session player is not a member, so there is no edge to put the capacity on. |". 01.03.01-membership-records-lifecycle.md:34 — the attribute table: "| **Capacity periods** | permanent / touring / staff / honorary, each with its own date range | Versioned, not overwritten (D-10) |". — VIOLATED BY — 01.03.01-membership-records-lifecycle.md:82 — the worked example in the Edge Cases table: "| **A member's capacity changes over time (roadie → sound engineer → member)** | **RESOLVED — one continuous tenure, versioned capacity periods** (D-10). Behaviorally: tenure is unbroken (one row, \"2015–present\"), capacity is a list (**\"crew 2015–2017, staff 2017–2020, permanent 2020–\"**), and any date-scoped query resolves against the capacity period, not the tenure. |"
findings.failureScenario: An implementer builds the capacity enum from D-03 as {permanent, touring, staff, honorary} and then cannot represent the file's own canonical example of the capacity-versioning feature — the roadie who becomes a sound engineer who becomes a member — because `crew` has no slot. They must either widen the enum (changing what 01.03.03 D-09's seed keys on, since a fifth non-seeded capacity now exists and must be classified) or silently remap `crew` to `staff`, which changes the displayed capacity history that D-10 exists to preserve verbatim. The enum is load-bearing well beyond this file: 01.03.03 D-09 keys the peer seed to it, 01.01.03 derives acting contexts from it, and 01.03.01 line 111 groups the lineup by it ('Permanent / Touring / Staff'). The removal of `session` (D-05) shows the enum is treated as closed and deliberately curated, so the extra value is an inconsistency rather than an open vocabulary.

findings.failureScenario: The tracking is malformed on both halves the rules care about: the deferral target names a stage (`/ideate-discover Step 5 deepening`) that has completed for this sub-domain, and the question it points at is not merely resolved but resolved so as to make the row's premise unreachable. An implementer or a downstream spec writer surveying open governance gaps records 'name ownership has no governance home for shared aliases' as live work, and either builds a governance-less alias name-ownership path that nothing can populate, or spends the reconciliation effort discovering it is moot. The substantive rule that replaces it — governance capture fires at alias creation and at solo-to-shared promotion (01.01.02 E-28, domain CX-12) — is stated nowhere in 01.04.02, which is the file that owns name ownership.

The index's own explanatory note justifies the denial on membership grounds that neither child's grant depends on.

findings.failureScenario: Both Operator grants are explicitly for a non-member Operator — the venue that must resolve which party a band name now points at before honouring a booking — so the index note's 'no standing in a band they are not part of' rationale does not reach them. An implementer or downstream spec writer building access control or navigation from the domain-level matrix (the pipeline key file that all downstream workflows read first, per the index header) denies Operators the name-resolution read that 01.04.02 and 01.04.04 both call load-bearing, and a venue books the wrong successor after a split. findings.claim: The 01.06 cross-cut file records the EPK snapshot-versus-live-view question as open and states that snapshotting 'survives as an option' under it, while 01.06.03 resolved that question in the negative and made never-snapshotting a decision.
findings.evidence: 01.06-portfolio-media-epk-cx.md:95 — Rejected Pair R-02: "| R-02 | 01.06.02 Credit-Backed Portfolio | 01.06.03 EPK (as a stored snapshot) | Considered snapshotting the portfolio into each EPK for stability. Rejected here as a *default*: staleness is the flaw the whole feature exists to remove (01.06.03 D-01). **It survives only as an option under 01.06.03 Q-01**, where the case is the narrow one of a pitch changing after it lands — not the general one. |". 01.06-portfolio-media-epk-cx.md:55 — CX-02 note 5: "A credit disputed between send and open. **Unresolved — 01.06.03 Q-01.**" (and note 2 at line 52 likewise frames Q-01 as a live hazard). — CONTRADICTED BY — 01.06.03-epk-generation-sharing.md:103 — "| Q-01 | ✅ RESOLVED (Step 5, D-05/DT-04): stay **live**, never snapshot; a send watches the foregrounded facts and notifies the sender on material change. |"; 01.06.03-epk-generation-sharing.md:96 — D-05: "EPK stays a live view; a send watches foregrounded facts and notifies the sender on material change"; 01.06.03-epk-generation-sharing.md:74 — DT-04: "❌ REJECTED. Snapshotting freezes the attested credits into a static claim — which is exactly a PDF, and forfeits the live-view advantage that is the whole reason to generate rather than author."
findings.failureScenario: An implementer scoping the EPK reads R-02 and builds an opt-in snapshot mode for the 'pitch changed after it landed' case, because R-02 states that option survives. 01.06.03 D-05 and DT-04 forbid it outright and replace it with a different mechanism entirely — a sender-side watch on foregrounded facts that fires a notification. The two produce different features, different data (a stored copy versus none), and different recipient experiences (a frozen kit versus current truth). The cross-cut file is where a downstream reader looks for the sub-domain's unresolved interactions, so a resolved question presented as open with a surviving alternative is the tracking failure that most reliably produces built-but-unwanted scope.
